newsitem.title: PANAMA: Colombians flee to Panama to escape violence.
newsitem.headline: Colombians flee to Panama to escape violence.

text.p: About 200 Colombians, mostly women, children and elderly, have fled to Panama to escape violence in northwest Colombia, a Panamanian official said on Wednesday..

"Church groups and the Red Cross are looking for clothes, medicine and food for these people who are fleeing violence and are now on Panamanian soil," Francisco Tang, substitute legislator for Panama's Darien province which borders Colombia, told reporters.
"The most dangerous thing to do is ignore the problem now," Tang said.

He said Panamanian officials suspected most of the Colombians came from the banana-growing Uraba region in Antioquia near the Panama border where four peasants were killed on Tuesday by suspected leftist guerrillas.
The area has long been the scene of bitter conflicts between rebels and right-wing paramilitary groups battling for control of lucrative contraband routes.
At least 14 people including leftist rebels and civilians died in fighting across Colombia in separate incidents on Tuesday.
